sections.html:
The Otsego County Register of Deeds is at 225 W Main Street, Gaylord, MI 49735. Call 989-731-7550 or fax 989-731-7519. The office holds every record of a transfer or encumbrance of land in the county.

Staff time stamp each paper, assign liber and page numbers and index it on computer. The computerized index and images start on March 5, 1864, and any record can be pulled and copied in the office within minutes. Images are also sold online.

The office works with the county Equalization Department to keep ownership current, using tax identification numbers or owner names. It does not run searches for the public. If you want a search done for you, call a title insurance company or a land records data company, or sit at the Gaylord counter and look for yourself.

The office charges $30 for each document it records, with every page included. That rate has applied since October 1, 2016.

Otsego County Register of Deeds fees
ServiceFee
Recording a document, all pages$30
Each extra instrument a document assigns or discharges$3
Copies of recorded instruments$1 per page
Certification of a document$5
Real estate record search$5 per name
State or federal tax lien certificate$3 per name
U.C.C.-11 certificate$6 per name

Of the recording fee, $4 goes to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation Fund. That share is skipped for fixture filings, state, federal and MESC liens, state deeds and plats. For mailed copy orders, phone 989-731-7551 first so staff can fix the page count and price. Payment is due when the service is performed, and checks are made out to Otsego County Register of Deeds.

Transfer tax is collected at the moment of recording, under MCL 207.505(5) and MCL 207.526(6). Either print the full consideration on the deed or file a real estate transfer valuation affidavit, which costs nothing. An exempt transfer should say so on its face.

The rates are $3.75 for the state and 55 cents for the county per $500 or fraction, from MCL 207.525 and MCL 207.504. Because a fraction counts as a whole block, a price that lands just past a $500 mark costs a little more than you might expect. Budget for the tax on your side of the closing statement.

Exemptions that matter to homeowners:

  • Consideration below $100 removes the tax under both acts.
  • A deed from a mortgage foreclosure skips the state tax, and one given on a government-backed loan skips both. The state exemption does not carry over to the lender's later sale of the property.
  • Deeds within a family, parent to child or grandparent to grandchild, are exempt from the state tax only.
  • A land contract owes nothing until the buyer finishes paying and legal title passes.
  • A deed that moves a boundary line with no money paid is exempt from both.

Mineral rights transfers and leases are exempt too, but they come up rarely in a house sale.

Otsego County offers electronic recording for people who file many documents at once. It is a secure, verified-user service, and you register through an approved provider before you start. Two providers are named: Simplifile, at simplifile.com, and CSC, at cscglobal.com/service/erecording.

Online, the office sells images of recorded documents. Searching the real estate record at the office costs $5 per name, and certificate searches for state tax liens, federal tax liens and U.C.C.-11 filings carry the per-name fees in the fee table.

Freedom of Information requests go on a completed FOIA Request Form sent by email to the county's FOIA coordinator or faxed to 989-731-7529. A deed copy does not need a FOIA request, since recorded instruments are available at $1 per page.

sections.h2: What a deed needs before it reaches the counter
sections.html:
Two statutes apply in Gaylord. MCL 565.201 governs how the paper looks, and MCL 211.135 governs proof that taxes are paid. A deed that misses either can be refused.

  • Legible black or dark blue signatures, with each signer's name printed below and matching the notary's wording.
  • The grantee's mailing address, plus whoever drafted the instrument with a business address.
  • Black type of at least 10 points on white 20-pound paper, between letter and legal size, and a clear 2.5 inches at the top of page one.
  • A single opening line naming the one recordable event, such as a warranty deed or a mortgage discharge.
  • Social Security numbers masked down to the last four digits, unless a law demands more.

With a covenant of warranty in the deed, the county treasurer must certify there are no tax liens or titles on the parcel and that five prior years of taxes are paid. A city, village or township treasurer certifies the local side. A quitclaim deed without warranty covenants, a sheriff's deed and a deed made under a court judgment are excused.

Otsego County is in Northern Michigan. Gaylord is the only city and the seat, and Vanderbilt is the lone village. Water shapes the housing stock: the county has more than 370 lakes, mostly in the south, and Otsego Lake is the largest at 1,972 acres. I-75 bypasses Gaylord on the west and M-32 runs east and west through it.

Population is estimated at 26,080, a gain of 3.9% since the 2020 count of 25,091. The middle home value is $219,700, owner occupancy is 77.2%, and monthly rent is $1,008. The county has 14,976 housing units but 11,231 households, so units outnumber households by about 3,700, which points to a lot of second homes and cabins. Building permits numbered 25 in 2025.

Owners of lake or woodland parcels can ask the Equalization Department for the parcel's tax identification number, and the Treasurer for the tax certificate, before choosing a closing date. A buyer who works remotely should confirm internet service at the address.

sections.h2: Step by step: recording a sale
sections.html:
Your title company normally handles recording, but the sequence is worth knowing, especially for a family or cash transfer.

  1. Get the parcel's tax identification number from the Equalization Department.
  2. Ask the county treasurer for the tax certificate if the deed has warranty covenants.
  3. Prepare the deed to the paper, margin and signature rules above.
  4. Print the price on the deed or attach the free valuation affidavit, and note any exemption.
  5. Deliver the deed with the $30 fee and the transfer tax, in person at 225 W Main Street or through an e-recording provider.

A cash buyer follows the same steps and pays the same charges. What a cash sale skips is the lender's appraisal and underwriting, not the recording. Call 989-731-7550 if a question comes up about a document before you send it.

faqs.q: What is the Otsego County recording fee?
faqs.a: Gaylord charges $30 a document with all pages included, and adds $3 for each extra instrument a single paper assigns or discharges.

faqs.q: Is there a filing fee for Otsego County's transfer valuation affidavit?
faqs.a: None. The county collects nothing for the affidavit, which you can use instead of printing the value on the deed.

faqs.q: How far back do Otsego County's computer records go?
faqs.a: They start on March 5, 1864. The office keeps both the index and the images on computer from that date to the present.

faqs.q: What do Otsego County copies cost?
faqs.a: Each page is $1, and a certification adds $5. For mail orders, ring the office first for an exact quote.

faqs.q: Will Gaylord staff search a title for me?
faqs.a: No. The office does not provide search services and points people to a title insurance company or a land records data company. You can search the records in person at the Gaylord office.
